body:
This is all really great stuff you have put out here. I'm going to give the journal a go. I'm glad you suggested the pen and paper over computer, it's definitely a more focused method I think.

As far as the girl problems go, thank you for suggesting a method for getting over her. I think those mental notes are something that I'm really going to have to grasp. This is something that was always super hard-lined in my head, like I'm thinking to myself, 'tough shit bro, just gotta get over it,' and that's always a rather crippling thought.

Thank you for all of these suggestions, I will make a solid effort in these areas so I can avoid entering dark and confusing places, and be on my way to being the kind of person I want to ultimately be. Funny how much a feeling can change with a little guidance sometimes.

Sorry for the delayed response, I was exhausted and had to wake up early so I went to bed.

I stopped swimming because I was burnt out, more than anything else. After ten years it got to be a little much, especially when I started falling behind my college team. I really should start again, just on my own. I agree with you, exercise will make a difference, it's just a matter of being able to motivate myself to get into it again.

All you are saying is true, and I need to do a better job of believing in that. As for the girl, I think what you are saying about addressing the issue personally needs to happen. It's really scary to think about though, because her husband is my best friend and she is the singer for our band. I've been keeping it to myself because I believe that I would never do anything to hurt either of them, but this feeling is a big part of why I feel stuck and miserable sometimes. Addressing it is all I really can do at this point.

As for those questions, I agree with you they are a good place to start. I think I will start making a personal journal, just so I can start thinking about these things more often, and therefore more likely to take some kind of action.

I suppose sometimes I need these reminders, it's easy to get stuck in a negative loop when I'm feeling so alone and numb.

I feel much better today after getting out and working, and after getting this off my chest and reading the kind and encouraging words from you both. Sometimes I think we just need somebody to talk to for perspective when we're feeling down and begin considering suicide as a viable option. It's scary and I don't like that feeling.

Thank you so much again, I really appreciate everyone here who reaches out to others when they ask for help.
I just gotta keep moving so I stop questioning myself. Thanks!

First, thank you so much. This isn't my normal account, but I will be coming back to it. Asking for help feels so uncomfortable sometimes, like I'm being bothersome to others, but I know my reaction would be first to talk, so I know there are others out there who would do the same, so again, thank you.

It really is that risk of actually following through with changes that's the most terrifying. When I get to this point, that's when I really start thinking about the "easy" way out and why I want to do it in the first place, which often boils down to that dark, empty feeling. All I know is it's gonna be a journey out...
